Part B
Situation
You are Gehry Zhang and you work for a property developer called Dragon Peak Properties (DPP). Your boss is Norman Kwok, a publicity and marketing manager. DPP is currently working on two projects: the Jade Islands, which have recently been completed and the Golden Flower Island development, which is in the planning process.
You will now listen to a radio panel show called Business Matters with host Charlie Meadows. Appearing on the show are Norman Kwok and Ann Lam from the environmental group Green Treasure.
Before the recording is played, you will have five minutes to study the Question-Answer Book and the Data File to familiarise yourself with the situation and the tasks.
Complete the tasks by following the instructions in the Question-Answer Book and on the recording. You will find all the information you need in the Question-Answer Book, the Data File and on the recording. As you listen, you can make notes on page 3 of the Data File.
You now have five minutes to familiarise yourself with the Question-Answer Book and the Data File.

Email from Norman Kwok to Gehry Zhang, 8 April
File　 Message　 Junk　 Delete　 Reply　 Reply All　 Forward　 Move　 Mark Unread　 Follow up
To: Gehry Zhang
From: Norman Kwok
Sent: Sat 8 April 9:05AM
Subject: Things for you to do
Hi Gehry
I need you to write the following for me.
First, as you will remember, I have a follow up meeting with Manu Architects on Monday to provide them with feedback on their initial concept plan for Golden Flower Adventure Mall. I asked our staff to send their comments to you, so you should have received these already. Please prepare a document for me indicating which features our staff say to keep and which not to keep from the initial concept plan. Also, summarise their opinions regarding how they would like to develop the features.
Second, write up an overview of what DPP has done in Hong Kong to protect the environment. Mention our recent achievements and what we are doing to protect the orchids and the butterflies on Golden Flower Island. This will be placed on our webpage in the section “Dragon Peak’s Commitment to the Environment in Hong Kong”. We want to reassure people that we are an environmentally friendly company.
Third, as a follow up to yesterday’s team meeting, write the invitation to Ms. Tse explaining what her role will be and what we would like her to do at the Opening Ceremony. She apparently often rejects invitations like this so you need to mention things that might persuade her to accept. Have a look at her PlinyPedia entry and see if any of her interests or beliefs specifically align with what we are doing.
Thank you for all your hard work.
Regards
Norman
Extract from Flora and Fauna of South China by J.R. Hartley
Golden Dragon Tail Butterfly
This butterfly is quite common in Asia but exists in only a very few areas of South China. It is the only known species in South China that pollinates the extremely rare Splash of Gold Orchid. This rare and beautiful plant can now only be found on Golden Flower Island. Only half of this island has been designated by the HKSAR Government as a nature park due to it being an area of special scientific interest. Development is therefore only restricted in that part of the island. Trouble may be brewing, however, as the local press has reported that development plans are afoot for the island for 2017. Let’s hope common sense prevails and we can protect these beautiful plants and creatures.

Email from Mari Nakamura to Gehry Zhang, 28 March
File　 Message　 Junk　 Delete　 Reply　 Reply All　 Forward　 Move　 Mark Unread　 Follow up
To: Gehry Zhang
From: Mari Nakamura
Sent: Tues 28 March 4:37PM
Subject: Initial Concept Plan
Gehry
My thoughts so far...
Love their concept so far. This will be an awesome space for a variety of exciting activities. The waterfall, the ship and the lake – yes, all great ideas and should be the key features of the mall. Tell them to drop the castle though.
I’d like to suggest including a swimming pool in the mall design. I’ve told Ripple from our team to send you her comments. She’s worked on several projects of a similar nature, so has some experience of this type of thing.
In order to maximize the potential activities within the central area of the mall, and in keeping with the overall jungle adventure theme, I’d suggest including ziplines over the swimming pool. I’ve included a stock photo to give you an idea of what I mean.
Stock photo: ziplines over a pool
Mari Nakamura Activities team leader

Email from Ripple Wu to Gehry Zhang, 29 March
File　 Message　 Junk　 Delete　 Reply　 Reply All　 Forward　 Move　 Mark Unread　 Follow up
To: Gehry Zhang
From: Ripple Wu
Sent: Wed 29 March 3:18PM
Subject: Golden Flower Adventure Mall
Hey Gehry
Their initial concept plan is definitely in line with what we had discussed initially, i.e. a jungle theme. Love it! I agree with Mari about the castle. Since when are there castles in a jungle?!
Personally, I’d go for making the lake an aquarium. Plus, the sailing ship can’t really fit both restaurants and shops really when you think about it practically, can it? So I’d say take out the shops.
As for the swimming pool idea, yes, I agree with Mari. We have worked on similar constructions in the UK in recent years particularly at the Highland Adventure Centre and the pool worked a treat there. As did the ziplines.
One idea to think about for the mall is this:
Example of abseiling near a waterfall
Obviously we could never have the general public abseiling actually in the waterfall like this guy!!!! It would have to be on the sides.
Cheers
Ripple

Alison Lo → Norman Kwok · Wed 5 April 2017 1:56PM
Dear Norman
Yes, I heard that a query had been raised on the Business Matters radio show. The solution at the Highland Adventure Centre was quite costly at the time and the centre was closed for six months. Substantial reconstruction work was carried out reducing the waterfall from 45 to 30 metres. At that height, the clouds did not form as they had previously. Since the reopening of the centre, no similar problems have occurred.
By the way, I didn’t get round to sending Gehry my recommendations, as I wanted to hear what everybody else was suggesting first. From our team’s perspective, all the features proposed in Manu Architects’ initial concept plan and in our staff’s suggestions are definitely all practical. Nothing that we haven’t done before.
Alison Lo Engineering team
Norman Kwok → Alison Lo · Wed 5 April 2017 1:14PM
Dear Alison
As you may have heard I was ambushed by that Ann Lam from Green Treasure on Business Matters on the radio this morning. Such a nasty woman! She was going on about that Highland Adventure Centre in the UK that caused us all the headaches a couple of years back. I remembered that we’d had problems but didn’t know the specifics. Can you remember how we resolved the issues?
Norman

Minutes from Golden Flower Adventure Mall team meeting
Golden Flower Adventure Mall team meeting
Date8:00 AM, Fri. 7 April 2017VenueThe Eyrie, Dragon Peak TowerChairpersonNorman KwokMembersAlison Lo · Mari Nakamura · Ripple WuSecretaryGehry ZhangOpening Ceremony of Mall
Dr Lo presented a progress report on construction work of the Golden Flower Adventure Mall. She confirmed that the provisional completion date of 30 November 2018 was still in place. A discussion ensued as to the best date for the opening ceremony to take place. 1 January 2019 was suggested as was leaving it until Lunar New Year. Finally it was decided that 24 December would be best as it would mean that the mall could immediately benefit from the holiday period over Christmas.
Mr Kwok reported the results of the opening ceremony budget proposal meeting with the Finance Department as follows:
Item
Requested budget
Approved?
Reason
Guest of honour fees
HK$100,000
✓
n/a
Horse and carriage for ceremony
HK$50,000
✕
Refused due to insurance concerns.
Possible activities at the Opening Ceremony were discussed given the Finance Department’s refusal of Item 2. Dr Lo suggested that if the guest of honour swam then he or she could be the first person to swim in the new pool as a way of declaring it open. All agreed. Ms Nakamura presented a selection of possible celebrities to be the guest of honour at the Opening Ceremony. From these it was decided to approach Ms Mariana Tse. All agreed. Gehry to contact her.
Ms Wu pointed out that Ms Mariana Tse was in the media recently for refusing to accept fees for a similar event. Mr Kwok suggested using the fees budget to make a donation to the charity of Ms Tse’s choice. All agreed. Gehry to include this.
Meeting ended at 8:40 am.
